2607.27283.title: Benchmarking the Residual: What Long-Horizon Evaluations Add Beyond Matched Short-Task Performance
2607.27283.paper_summary: Long-horizon benchmarks often show that agents fail more as tasks become longer. This observation is useful for deployment, but it does not by itself explain why failure occurs. More stages create more opportunities for ordinary errors to compound; longer tasks may also contain harder individual decisions or become harder as conversation history, tool outputs, and environment changes accumulate. We use trajectory-induced degradation to mean this last possibility: earlier execution makes later work harder. When the harmful accumulation is specifically the text visible to the model, it is often called context rot. In this position paper, we argue that to claim a "long-horizon failure", benchmarks must compare actual full-task success against a baseline prediction built from short, individual stages. We call the log-ratio between this prediction and actual success the horizon residual. The comparison must use the same agent configuration and specify in advance how stages, checkpoints, information, and budgets will be chosen. The residual shows that the full rollout differs from the chosen baseline; targeted experiments are still needed to explain why.
2607.27283.paper_summary_zh: 長期基準通常顯示，隨著任務變長，代理的失敗率會增加。這一觀察對於部署是有用的，但它本身並不能解釋為什麼會發生失敗。更多的階段創造了更多普通錯誤累積的機會；更長的任務可能還包含更難的個別決策，或者隨著對話歷史、工具輸出和環境變化的累積而變得更難。我們使用「軌跡引起的退化」來指代這最後一種可能性：早期的執行使得後期的工作變得更困難。當有害的累積特別是模型可見的文本時，通常稱之為上下文腐爛。在這篇立場文件中，我們主張要聲稱「長期失敗」，基準必須將實際的全任務成功與基於短期、個別階段所建立的基準預測進行比較。我們稱這個預測與實際成功之間的對數比率為「視野殘差」。比較必須使用相同的代理配置，並提前指定如何選擇階段、檢查點、信息和預算。殘差顯示全過程與所選基準的不同；仍然需要有針對性的實驗來解釋原因。
